episode.subject: shaggy mane fungus
episode.title: The ground went past
episode.body:
I was letting the edge of my cap go a little at a time.

Then wind came out of a tube. My stalk folded. A leaf caught against me, and we scraped through the grass together.

When we stopped, my gills were facing the sky.

proposals.admission: Proposed only; independent image/prose/canon review required
proposals.visualReview: Individually opened exact published large image. Grassy verge is strewn with snapped, bent and fallen pale stems with black mature cap remains. Foreground right shows exposed purple-dark gills; fallen leaves are interspersed. Young white upright mushrooms remain farther back. No leaf blower, person or active gust is pictured; observer description attributes the aftermath to a leaf blower.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Observer-recorded machine disturbance is factual source context. Lionel, a specific gust folding his stalk, contact with one leaf, joint scraping and the final first-person orientation are fictional reconstruction. The image carries fallen mature mushrooms, leaves and exposed gills, not every motion. No conscious decision to shed tissue, pain measurement or sentient leaf is scientific fact.
proposals.canon: Later than admitted40 mature dissolving cap. Rooted fungal individual speaks through its physically displaced fruiting body; do not make young remaining caps his renewed body. No whole-mycelium death or regeneration claim. Existing Michigan grassy woodland-margin home preserved with a maintained path edge as fictional setting; real source is a California campus, not his literal travel history.
proposals.proseReview: A gradual loss of cap becomes sudden displacement; his downward-facing reproductive surface ends facing open sky. No reassurance of younger caps, greater-height vanity, sap generosity, warmth or explicit moral. One leaf is caught debris, not prey or a tenant being accommodated. Disturbance is not used as a suffering punchline.
proposals.reviewRisk: Wide documentary aftermath rather than isolated macro. Lead must judge whether the foreground exposed gills and scattered stems clear the visual bar; do not approve because the event is unusual alone.
